Director of Product, Workflows CreatorIQ is the software enterprise brands and agencies run their creator marketing programs on. A large customer works with thousands of creators a year across dozens of programs and several markets, and every one of those partnerships has to be sourced, vetted, agreed, briefed, tracked and paid for. You'll own that operational core and lead the product teams that cover it today, accountable for making the whole thing feel like one operation instead of a series of handoffs. The mandate is to rebuild that operation around AI. Tooling in this category, ours included, was designed for a world where a person did each step by hand, and it still assumes that. It scales by adding people. A community manager keeping a 2,000-creator program on track lives in spreadsheets. An agency casting 300 creators against a brief in a week gets there by throwing bodies at it. Your job is to change what the software is responsible for, so programs scale without the headcount and the people running them spend their time on decisions that need judgment. In this role, you’ll get to: Own the workflow end to end. Discovery, Lists, Community, Campaigns and Messaging are one continuous job for our customers, and today they feel like separate products. Making them one, and making most of it happen without a human clicking through it, is the mandate. Lead and grow a team of product managers. You'll set the bar for how they work, coach them on discovery and judgment, and give them enough room to own their surfaces without you in the middle of every decision. Decide what gets rebuilt agentically, what gets simplified, and what gets deleted. Plenty of our existing workflow exists because someone needed a manual solution in 2020. Some of it should be automated, some should be replaced by a better model of the problem, and some should just go away. Get the trust model right. Provenance, confidence, human-in-the-loop review, honest failure, and clean rollback are what decide whether an enterprise customer lets an agent touch a live campaign. description: Zwei Marken. Viele Ideen. Und du bringst sie in die Umsetzung. leevje und I AM EDITIONS stehen für Mode, Ästhetik und eine starke Community. Du organisierst Shootings und koordinierst interne sowie externe Content-Ressourcen und UGC-Creator. Du planst und erstellst unsere Newsletter in Klaviyo und entwickelst Kampagnen, Segmente und automatisierte Flows weiter. Du planst und setzt unsere WhatsApp-Kommunikation um. Du pflegst Produkte und Inhalte in Shopify , legst neue Produkte an und erstellst Produkt-, Launch- und Shoptexte. Du aktualisierst Collections, Landingpages und Shopinhalte rund um unsere Drops. Du sorgst dafür, dass Kampagnen nicht nur geplant, sondern auch sauber und pünktlich umgesetzt werden. Je nach Erfahrung und Interesse kannst du weitere Bereiche wie Paid-Social-Creatives und Performance Marketing mit übernehmen. Du übernimmst Verantwortung und denkst selbstständig die nächsten Schritte mit. Du hast ein gutes ästhetisches Gespür für Mode, Bildsprache und Marken. These decisions shape real-world outcomes. Whether rockets successfully launch into space, autonomous vehicles make it to market, or communities recover after major storms. Until now, insurance has made billion-pound decisions using outdated tools. We're changing that. Our platform brings together data, AI, and human expertise to give insurers the fastest path from submission to decision, helping them move faster, act smarter, and take on more risk with confidence. Backed by a16z, Highland Europe, and Battery Ventures, we're scaling globally. We're already trusted by nearly 50 of the world's largest insurers, with zero churn and billions in premiums flowing through hx. What makes hx different is the people who build it. Impact isn't tied to title or tenure. It's defined by the challenges you take on and the discipline you bring. Surrounded by peers who stretch you, you'll do the best, hardest work of your life in a company engineered to endure. If that sounds like you, join us in building what comes next. title: Network Developer
description: Senior Network Developer About Share Share is the global marketplace for bandwidth. We aggregate telco infrastructure across Africa (fiber routes, subsea capacity, data centers, cloud on-ramps) into a single intelligence layer. That lets ISPs, hyperscalers and AI companies get connectivity where they need it in seconds, not months. Today, bandwidth is bought and sold through slow, private, one-off deals, with almost no price transparency. We're replacing that with one neutral exchange: an API on top of real infrastructure, with prices set by actual supply and demand. It's already live across East Africa, with thousands of kilometers of fiber, 12 infrastructure providers, 10 data centers, and around 8 million people served. The Role Our network is the foundation of the product. Every route a customer provisions through our API has to exist, perform and stay up on real hardware. We're hiring a Senior Network Developer to design and build that network as software: a distributed, multi-provider fabric that engineers change through code, not by logging into devices. You'll own the network architecture end to end. That covers our BGP edge (transit, peering at KIXP and LINX, private interconnects with hyperscalers), the backbone, and the PoPs and data centers we're adding across the continent. You'll set the standards our network is built to, which partner ISPs connecting to us will inherit. As we grow, you'll also help build the network engineering team. What you'll do Design the backbone and PoP architecture as standard, repeatable building blocks, from edge to data center, so we can add capacity and new markets without redesigning each time. Drive our move to Segment Routing and a clean IP architecture, including IPv4 reuse, IPv6, and how customer and internal address space coexist. Build on disaggregated white-box hardware (Edgecore with IP Infusion OcNOS today), and make the hardware and software calls that keep us fast and affordable. Turn operations into software. That means a source of truth (Nautobot), templated config (Jinja), and CI/CD with validation, staged rollouts and rollback for every change. Build the telemetry and observability that show what the network is really doing. Use AI where it actually helps: anomaly detection, automated triage, and auto-remediation with a human in the loop. Own availability. Limit how much any failure can affect, mitigate first and diagnose second, and turn post-mortems into fixes in the system. Work with our software team on the API and provisioning layer that exposes the network to customers, and with partner ISPs' engineers on the hand-off. Help hire and develop the engineers who'll run this with you. Our Ideal Candidate 8+ years building and operating large networks at a hyperscaler, CDN, internet exchange, carrier or ISP. Deep BGP at scale: route policy, communities, RPKI, traffic engineering, peering and transit. Strong data center and backbone design. You know Clos/EVPN-VXLAN fabrics and MPLS or Segment Routing, and when each makes sense. Hands-on with white-box or disaggregated networking, including choosing hardware and knowing where the silicon limits you. You treat the network as code. You write automation yourself (Python or similar), and you've built or run the pipelines, source of truth and telemetry that make that safe. You've owned availability for something that couldn't go down, and can walk us through a real incident: what broke, how you found it, and what you changed. AI-native in how you work. You've built with these tools, not just used them, and you have a view on where they help in operations and where they don't. You think like an owner. You bring ideas, not tickets, and you want to help build a team, not just a network. A clear, direct communicator who's comfortable with partners' engineers and with our founders. Nice to have Experience at an internet exchange, or running peering at scale. Open networking stacks like SONiC, OcNOS or FRR, or contributions to them
